records.source: בְּעֶשְׂרִ֣ים וְחָמֵ֣שׁ שָׁנָ֣ה לְ֠גָלוּתֵנוּ בְּרֹ֨אשׁ הַשָּׁנָ֜ה בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֗דֶשׁ בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר בְּעֶ֣צֶם׀הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֗ה הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד־יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: In [the] twenty and five year of our exile, at [the] beginning of the year, on the tenth of the month, in [the] fourteenth year after that the city was struck, on the very same day was upon me [the] hand of Yahweh, and he brought me there.
pieces: On the tenth day of the month at the start of the year, in the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the fourteenth year after the city had fallen, on that very day the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me there.

L.1: In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the head of the year, on the tenth of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck, on this same day the hand of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was upon me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me there.

R.1: It was the twenty-fifth year of our exile, the tenth day of the month at the beginning of the year. It was fourteen years after Jerusalem had been captured. On that very day the power of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on me, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me there.

decisions.choice: the twenty-fifth year of our exile, fourteen years after the city fell: 573 BC
decisions.reason: Ezekiel counts from the exile of King Jehoiachin in 597 BC, as in 1:2. The twenty-fifth year is 573 BC, fourteen years after Jerusalem was taken in 587/586 BC (33:21). It is the latest date in the book apart from 29:17. The date is worked out from the book's own reckoning and is the one usually given.

decisions.choice: at the beginning of the year: the start of the year, which may mean the first month in spring or the seventh month in autumn
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase is the one later used for the New Year festival. Israel's calendar counted the months from the spring (Exodus 12:2), but a year could also be reckoned from the autumn. The text does not say which is meant here; on the spring reckoning the tenth day is the day the Passover lamb was chosen (Exodus 12:3), and on the autumn reckoning it is the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 25:9), when a jubilee year began.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me: the LORD's power took hold of him
decisions.reason: As in 1:3, 8:1 and 37:1, the phrase introduces a vision that comes on the prophet by the LORD's power. This is the last of the great visions of the book, and it answers the vision of chapters 8-11, where the glory left the temple.

decisions.choice: the hand of the LORD was upon me (L); came on me (B); the power of the LORD came on me (R)
decisions.reason: The book's formula, as in 1:3 and 37:1.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "The city" is Jerusalem (33:21). Readable names it.

records.heading: The vision of the new temple

records.source: בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים הֱבִיאַ֖נִי אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי אֶל־הַ֤ר גָּבֹ֨הַּ֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְעָלָ֥יו כְּמִבְנֵה־עִ֖יר מִנֶּֽגֶב׃
records.gloss: In visions of God he brought me to [the] land of Israel and set me down on a mountain high very, and on it [was] like [the] structure of a city from [the] south.
pieces: In visions from God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the land of Israel and placed me on a very high mountain. On it, toward the south, was something like the buildings of a city.

L.2: In visions of God {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a mountain, very high, and on it [was something] like the structure of a city, on the south.

R.2: In visions from God, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took me to the land of Israel. He put me down on a very high mountain. On the south side of it I saw what looked like the buildings of a city.

decisions.choice: in visions of God: in visions that God gave
decisions.reason: The same words open the visions of 1:1 and 8:3. What follows is seen in a vision; Ezekiel is not taken bodily to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: a very high mountain: the temple mount raised up
decisions.reason: Mount Zion is not a very high mountain, but the prophets picture the LORD's mountain raised above all others (Isaiah 2:2; Micah 4:1). In Revelation 21:10 John is carried "to a great, high mountain" and shown the holy city; the whole of Revelation 21 draws on these chapters.

decisions.choice: like the structure of a city, on the south: the buildings Ezekiel sees from where he is set down
decisions.reason: Ezekiel stands on the mountain and sees, to the south of where he is, a walled complex that looks like a city. It is the temple area he is about to tour. The hedge "like" is Ezekiel's usual care in describing a vision (1:28).

decisions.choice: visions from God (B, R)
decisions.reason: As 8:3 at Balanced and Readable. Literal keeps "visions of God".

decisions.choice: it looked like the buildings of a city
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the hedge "looked like".

records.source: וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ מַרְאֵ֨הוּ֙ כְּמַרְאֵ֣ה נְחֹ֔שֶׁת וּפְתִיל־פִּשְׁתִּ֥ים בְּיָד֖וֹ וּקְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֑ה וְה֥וּא עֹמֵ֖ד בַּשָּֽׁעַר׃
records.gloss: And he brought me there, and look, a man, his appearance like [the] appearance of bronze, and a cord of linen in his hand and the reed of measurement, and he [was] standing in the gate.
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me there, I saw a man who looked like bronze. He had a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand, and he was standing in the gateway.

L.3: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought me there, and look, [there was] a man whose appearance [was] like the appearance of bronze, with a cord of linen and a measuring reed in his hand; and he was standing in the gate.

R.3: He took me there, and I saw a man who shone like bronze. He was holding a linen cord and a measuring stick. He was standing in the gateway.

decisions.choice: a cord of linen and the measuring reed: a line for long distances and a rod for buildings
decisions.reason: The cord measures long stretches, as in 47:3. The reed is a measuring rod of fixed length (verse 5). The measuring of the city shows that it is the LORD's and that it will be built (Zechariah 2:5-6; Jeremiah 31:39). In Revelation 11:1 and 21:15 John is given a measuring rod.

decisions.choice: a man whose appearance was like bronze: a heavenly guide, not the LORD
decisions.reason: The man shines like the burnished bronze of the living creatures in 1:7. He guides Ezekiel and explains what he sees, but he is distinct from the LORD who speaks from the temple in 43:6, so he is not spoken of with the pronouns used for God.

decisions.choice: gateway (B, R)
decisions.reason: The man stands in the passage of the gate building that the chapter goes on to measure; "gateway" makes that clear.

decisions.choice: measuring stick (R)
decisions.reason: The reed is a measuring rod, not a plant. Readable says what it was used for.

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר אֵלַ֜י הָאִ֗ישׁ בֶּן־אָדָ֡ם רְאֵ֣ה בְעֵינֶיךָ֩ וּבְאָזְנֶ֨יךָ שְּׁמָ֜ע וְשִׂ֣ים לִבְּךָ֗ לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִי֙ מַרְאֶ֣ה אוֹתָ֔ךְ כִּ֛י לְמַ֥עַן הַרְאוֹתְכָ֖ה הֻבָ֣אתָה הֵ֑נָּה הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And spoke to me the man, Son of man, see with your eyes and with your ears hear and set your heart to all that I [am] showing you, for in order to show you you have been brought here. Tell all that you [are] seeing to [the] house of Israel.
pieces: The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully, listen closely, and give your mind to everything I will show you. You were brought here so that I could show it to you. Tell the house of Israel everything you see."

L.4: And the man spoke to me: "Son of man, see with your eyes and with your ears hear, and set your heart to all that I am showing you, for you have been brought here in order that [I might] show [it to] you. Declare all that you are seeing to the house of Israel."

R.4: The man said to me, "Son of man, look carefully and listen closely. Pay attention to everything I show you. That is why you were brought here. Tell the people of Israel everything you see."

decisions.choice: see with your eyes, hear with your ears, set your heart: pay full attention
decisions.reason: The three commands together call for close attention of eye, ear and mind. The heart is the seat of thought and will. The same words return in 44:5, where the LORD gives the laws of the temple.

decisions.choice: tell the house of Israel: the vision is a message for the exiles
decisions.reason: Ezekiel sees the temple so that he can describe it to Israel. 43:10-11 says why: so that they will be ashamed of their sins and keep the temple's design and laws.

decisions.choice: son of man (all levels)
decisions.reason: As everywhere in the book (see 2:1).

decisions.choice: look carefully, listen closely, pay attention (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the eyes, ears and heart. Balanced and Readable say what the commands mean.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֥ה חוֹמָ֛ה מִח֥וּץ לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב וּבְיַ֨ד הָאִ֜ישׁ קְנֵ֣ה הַמִּדָּ֗ה שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֤וֹת בָּֽאַמָּה֙ וָטֹ֔פַח וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־רֹ֤חַב הַבִּנְיָן֙ קָנֶ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד וְקוֹמָ֖ה קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And look, a wall from outside to the house all around all around, and in the hand of the man [the] reed of measurement, six cubits by the cubit and a handbreadth; and he measured the breadth of the structure, one reed, and the height, one reed.
pieces: There was a wall all around the outside of the temple area. The measuring reed in the man's hand was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} long; each of its six cubits was a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the wall, and it was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} thick and {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} high.

L.5: And look, [there was] a wall on the outside of the house, all the way around, and in the man's hand [was] the measuring reed, six cubits [long], by the cubit and a handbreadth. And he measured the thickness of the structure, one reed, and the height, one reed.

R.5: A wall went all the way around the outside of the temple area. The man's measuring stick was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} long. He measured the wall. It was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} thick and {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} high.

decisions.choice: a cubit and a handbreadth: a long cubit, about 21 inches
decisions.reason: A common cubit was the length from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger, about 18 inches, and was reckoned as six handbreadths. Ezekiel's measuring cubit is a handbreadth longer, seven handbreadths, about 21 inches. This is the older "royal" cubit, known in Egypt and from 2 Chronicles 3:3, which speaks of cubits "by the former measure". So the reed of six such cubits is about 10 1/2 feet. All the measurements of chapters 40-48 use this cubit (43:13).

decisions.choice: the breadth of the structure: the thickness of the wall
decisions.reason: "Structure" here is the wall itself. Its breadth is its thickness from front to back. The wall is as thick as it is high, a solid barrier between the holy and the common (42:20).

decisions.choice: the measures in feet on the long cubit, with the cubits as the alternative (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the cubits of the Hebrew. Balanced and Readable give each measure in feet on the long cubit of verse 5 (about 21 inches), with the cubits as the reader's alternative (Measures setting). The span uses words for the alternative: "a reed", "fifty cubits".

decisions.choice: each of its six cubits was a cubit and a handbreadth (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the definition of the long cubit in the text. Readable leaves it to the measure in feet and to the footnote.

records.source: וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל־שַׁ֨עַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנָיו֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֔ימָה וַיַּ֖עַל בְּמַֽעֲלוֹתָ֑יו וַיָּ֣מָד׀אֶת־סַ֣ף הַשַּׁ֗עַר קָנֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ רֹ֔חַב וְאֵת֙ סַ֣ף אֶחָ֔ד קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד רֹֽחַב׃
records.gloss: And he went to [the] gate whose face [was] [the] way of the east, and he went up on its steps and measured the threshold of the gate, one reed breadth, and the threshold one, one reed breadth.
pieces: Then he went to the gate that faces east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate: it was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep. The other threshold was also {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep.

L.6: Then he went to the gate that faces toward the east, and went up its steps, and measured the threshold of the gate, one reed deep, and the other threshold, one reed deep.

R.6: Then he went to the east gate. He climbed its steps and measured the doorway at the front of the gate. It was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep. The other doorway was also {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep.

decisions.choice: the gate that faces east: the gate by which the glory will return
decisions.reason: The tour begins at the east gate. It is the gate by which the glory of the LORD left in 10:19 and 11:23, and by which it will return in 43:1-4; 44:1-2 then says it is to stay shut.

decisions.choice: and the threshold one, one reed deep: the clause repeats the measure
alternatives: a repetition, perhaps a copying slip
decisions.reason: The second clause seems to repeat the first, and it is missing from the Septuagint. It may be a copying slip, or it may name a second threshold, the inner one of verse 7. The translation keeps it as "the other threshold".

decisions.choice: threshold: the paved floor of the gate's doorway, measured from front to back
decisions.reason: The threshold is not a step but the whole floor of the opening, here one reed deep.

decisions.choice: doorway (R)
decisions.reason: Readable calls the deep threshold a doorway, which is what the reader would see.

records.source: וְהַתָּ֗א קָנֶ֨ה אֶחָ֥ד אֹ֨רֶךְ֙ וְקָנֶ֤ה אֶחָד֙ רֹ֔חַב וּבֵ֥ין הַתָּאִ֖ים חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וְסַ֣ף הַ֠שַּׁעַר מֵאֵ֨צֶל אוּלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֛עַר מֵֽהַבַּ֖יִת קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And the alcove one reed length and one reed breadth, and between the alcoves five cubits; and [the] threshold of the gate beside [the] porch of the gate from the house, one reed.
pieces: Each alcove was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} long and {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} wide, and the walls between the alcoves were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick. The threshold of the gate next to the porch of the gate, on the inner side, was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep.

L.7: And the alcove [was] one reed long and one reed wide, and between the alcoves [were] five cubits; and the threshold of the gate beside the porch of the gate on the inside, one reed.

R.7: Each alcove along the passage was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} long and {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} wide. The walls between the alcoves were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick. The doorway at the inner end of the gate, next to its porch, was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} deep.

decisions.choice: alcove: a recess in the wall of the gate passage, perhaps a guardroom
decisions.reason: The word is rare outside Ezekiel's temple; elsewhere it is used for the guardroom of the palace in 1 Kings 14:28 and 2 Chronicles 12:11. Here it names the recesses, three on each side (verse 10), that open off the gate passage. Gates of this plan, with three recesses on each side, have been found at Megiddo, Hazor and Gezer, where they served as guardrooms; whether these were for guards or for something else is not said.

decisions.choice: porch: the hall or vestibule at the end of the gate passage
decisions.reason: The word names a roofed entrance hall in front of a building. 1 Kings 6:3 uses it for the porch in front of Solomon's temple, and 8:16 for the same place in the temple Ezekiel saw defiled. Here, and through chapters 40-48, it is used for both the vestibule at the inner end of each gate and the porch of the temple itself (40:48). Its exact form, open with pillars or a closed hall, is uncertain.

decisions.choice: from the house: on the side toward the temple, the inner end
decisions.reason: "From the house" places the inner threshold and porch at the end of the gate nearest the temple.

decisions.choice: porch (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same English as 8:16 and 1 Kings 6:3, so that the reader can see that the porch of Ezekiel's temple answers to the one he saw defiled in chapter 8. It is used for every porch in chapters 40-48.

records.source: וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־אֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֛עַר מֵהַבַּ֖יִת קָנֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] porch of the gate from the house, one reed.
pieces: He measured the porch of the gate on the inner side: it was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}}.

L.8: And he measured the porch of the gate on the inside, one reed.

R.8: He measured the porch on the inner side of the gate. It was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}}.

decisions.choice: verse 8: the porch measured as one reed, against eight cubits in verse 9
decisions.reason: Verse 8 gives the porch one reed, but verse 9 gives it eight cubits. Many Hebrew manuscripts lack verse 8, and the Septuagint does not have it in this form, so it may be a scribe's repetition of the end of verse 7. The translation keeps the received text.

records.source: וַיָּ֜מָד אֶת־אֻלָ֤ם הַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ שְׁמֹנֶ֣ה אַמּ֔וֹת וְאֵילָ֖יו שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֑וֹת וְאֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֖עַר מֵהַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] porch of the gate, eight cubits, and its jambs, two cubits; and [the] porch of the gate [was] from the house.
pieces: Then he measured the porch of the gate: it was {{units:about 14 feet|eight cubits}} deep, and its jambs were {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} thick. The porch of the gate faced the temple.

L.9: Then he measured the porch of the gate, eight cubits, and its jambs, two cubits; and the porch of the gate [was] on the inside.

R.9: Then he measured the porch of the gate. It was {{units:about 14 feet|eight cubits}} deep. Its side posts were {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} thick. The porch was at the end of the gate nearest the temple.

decisions.choice: jambs: the thick walls or pilasters on each side of an opening
decisions.reason: The word (plural *'elim*) is used in these chapters for the projecting walls at the sides of the gate's openings and of the porch. It may mean side pillars, door posts or pilasters. The exact form is uncertain, but it is something solid that stands on either side of a doorway.

decisions.choice: jambs (L, B); side posts (R)
decisions.reason: The same English is used for this word throughout chapters 40-48. Readable says "side posts", a plainer word for the same thing.

records.source: וְתָאֵ֨י הַשַּׁ֜עַר דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֗ים שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה מִפֹּה֙ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה מִפֹּ֔ה מִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֖ת לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּ֑ם וּמִדָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לָאֵילִ֖ם מִפֹּ֥ה וּמִפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [the] alcoves of the gate [the] way of the east, three from here and three from here; one measure for the three of them, and one measure for the jambs from here and from here.
pieces: The east gate had three alcoves on each side. All three were the same size, and the jambs on each side were the same size.

L.10: And the alcoves of the gate toward the east [were] three on one side and three on the other; the three of them [had] one measure, and the jambs on either side [had] one measure.

R.10: Inside the east gate there were three alcoves on each side of the passage. They were all the same size. The side posts on both sides were also the same size.

decisions.choice: three alcoves on each side: a six-chambered gate
decisions.reason: Gates with three recesses on each side of the passage were built in Israel in the time of the kings (see the note on verse 7). The plan of Ezekiel's gate fits a real kind of city gate.

decisions.choice: on each side (B, R)
decisions.reason: "From here and from here" means on both sides of the passage.

records.source: וַיָּ֛מָד אֶת־רֹ֥חַב פֶּֽתַח־הַשַּׁ֖עַר עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּ֑וֹת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַשַּׁ֔עַר שְׁל֥וֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה אַמּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] breadth of [the] entrance of the gate, ten cubits; [the] length of the gate, thirteen cubits.
pieces: He measured the width of the gate's entrance: it was {{units:about 17 1/2 feet|ten cubits}}; and the gateway was {{units:about 22 3/4 feet|thirteen cubits}} long.

L.11: And he measured the breadth of the gate's entrance, ten cubits; the gate's length, thirteen cubits.

R.11: He measured the opening of the gate. It was {{units:about 17 1/2 feet|ten cubits}} wide. The gateway was {{units:about 22 3/4 feet|thirteen cubits}} long.

decisions.choice: the length of the gate, thirteen cubits: perhaps the width of the passage, or of the roofed part of it
alternatives: the roofed part of the entrance
decisions.reason: The gate is fifty cubits long (verse 15), so thirteen cubits cannot be its full length. It may be the width of the passage between the alcoves, or of the part of the entrance covered by a roof. The text does not explain it.

records.source: וּגְב֞וּל לִפְנֵ֤י הַתָּאוֹת֙ אַמָּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאַמָּה־אַחַ֥ת גְּב֖וּל מִפֹּ֑ה וְהַתָּ֕א שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֣וֹת מִפּ֔וֹ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And a barrier before the alcoves, one cubit, and one cubit [the] barrier from here; and the alcove six cubits from here and six cubits from here.
pieces: In front of the alcoves was a barrier {{units:about 21 inches|a cubit}} high on each side, and the alcoves were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} square on each side.

L.12: And a barrier in front of the alcoves, one cubit [on one side], and one cubit the barrier on the other; and the alcove [was] six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other.

R.12: In front of the alcoves on each side there was a low wall {{units:about 21 inches|a cubit}} high. The alcoves were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} on each side.

decisions.choice: barrier: a low wall or curb in front of the alcoves
decisions.reason: The word means a border or boundary. Here it marks off the alcoves from the passage, perhaps a low wall a cubit high or a ledge a cubit deep. The text gives one measure and does not say which.

decisions.choice: six cubits on this side and on that: each alcove was a reed square
decisions.reason: Six cubits is one reed, the size given in verse 7.

decisions.choice: low wall (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "barrier". Readable calls it a low wall, the likely sense (m1).

records.source: וַיָּ֣מָד אֶת־הַשַּׁ֗עַר מִגַּ֤ג הַתָּא֙ לְגַגּ֔וֹ רֹ֕חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְחָמֵ֖שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת פֶּ֖תַח נֶ֥גֶד פָּֽתַח׃
records.gloss: And he measured the gate from [the] roof of the alcove to its roof, breadth twenty and five cubits, entrance before entrance.
pieces: He measured the gate from the roof of one alcove to the roof of the alcove opposite: the width was {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}}, from one opening to the opening facing it.

L.13: And he measured the gate from the roof of [one] alcove to its roof [on the other side], a width of twenty-five cubits, opening facing opening.

R.13: He measured the width of the gate from the back of the alcoves on one side to the back of the alcoves on the other side. It was {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}} across, from one doorway to the doorway facing it.

decisions.choice: from the roof of the alcove to its roof: the full width of the gate building
alternatives: from the back wall of one alcove to the back wall of the other
decisions.reason: The measure runs across the gate, from the back of an alcove on one side to the back of the one opposite, over the passage. The alcoves are six cubits deep each, and the passage ten wide; with the walls, the whole is twenty-five cubits. Some take "roof" to mean the back wall or to read "back" here (as in the Septuagint).

decisions.choice: entrance before entrance: the doors of the alcoves face each other
decisions.reason: Each alcove opened onto the passage, opposite the one across from it.

decisions.choice: from the back of the alcoves on one side to the back of the alcoves on the other side (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what was being measured (m1).

records.source: וַיַּ֥עַשׂ אֶת־אֵילִ֖ים שִׁשִּׁ֣ים אַמָּ֑ה וְאֶל־אֵיל֙ הֶֽחָצֵ֔ר הַשַּׁ֖עַר סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he made jambs sixty cubits, and to [the] jamb of the court the gate all around all around.
pieces: He also measured the jambs: {{units:about 105 feet|sixty cubits}}. The gate reached to the jamb of the court on every side.

L.14: And he made the jambs sixty cubits, and the gate [reached] to the jamb of the court all around.

R.14: He measured the side posts too. They were {{units:about 105 feet|sixty cubits}}. The gate went all the way to the side post of the courtyard.

decisions.choice: he made the jambs sixty cubits: the verse is hard to understand
alternatives: the total length of the jambs together
decisions.reason: "He made" is unexpected where every other verse has "he measured", and no jamb could be sixty cubits high or wide in a gate fifty cubits long. The Septuagint reads "twenty cubits" and has a different text for the rest of the verse. The figure may be the total length of the jambs along the gate's walls, or the text may have been damaged. The translation follows the received text and reads "made" as "measured".

decisions.choice: measured (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "made", but the verse belongs to the measuring of the gate. Balanced and Readable read it in that sense; Literal keeps "made".

decisions.choice: jambs (L, B); side posts (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

records.source: וְעַ֗ל פְּנֵי֙ הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָֽאִית֔וֹן עַל־לִפְנֵ֕י אֻלָ֥ם הַשַּׁ֖עַר הַפְּנִימִ֑י חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And from [the] face of the gate, the entrance, to [the] face of [the] porch of the gate, the inner, fifty cubits.
pieces: From the front of the gate at the entrance to the far end of the porch on the inner side was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}}.

L.15: And from the front of the gate at the entrance to the front of the porch of the inner gate, fifty cubits.

R.15: From the front of the gate to the far end of its inner porch was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}}.

decisions.choice: from the front of the gate to the porch on the inside: the whole length of the gate building
decisions.reason: The gate is fifty cubits long, from its outer entrance to the inner face of its porch. "The inner gate" here is the inner end of the same gate, not the gate of the inner court.

records.source: וְחַלֹּנ֣וֹת אֲטֻמ֣וֹת אֶֽל־הַתָּאִ֡ים וְאֶל֩ אֵלֵיהֵ֨מָה לִפְנִ֤ימָה לַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֔יב וְכֵ֖ן לָאֵֽלַמּ֑וֹת וְחַלּוֹנ֞וֹת סָבִ֤יב׀סָבִיב֙ לִפְנִ֔ימָה וְאֶל־אַ֖יִל תִּמֹרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And closed windows to the alcoves and to their jambs within the gate all around all around, and so to the porches; and windows all around all around within, and to [the] jamb palm trees.
pieces: The alcoves and their jambs had recessed windows facing the inside of the gate all around, and so did the porch. There were windows all around on the inside, and the jambs were decorated with palm trees.

L.16: And [there were] recessed windows for the alcoves and for their jambs on the inside of the gate, all around, and likewise for the porches; and windows all around on the inside, and on the jambs [were] palm trees.

R.16: The alcoves and their side posts had windows set deep in their frames. They looked onto the inside of the gate all around. The porch also had windows like these. The side posts were decorated with carved palm trees.

decisions.choice: recessed windows: windows set in narrowing frames, or closed with lattices
decisions.reason: The word describing the windows means "closed" or "narrowed". 1 Kings 6:4 uses a similar phrase for the windows of Solomon's temple. They may be windows whose frames narrow toward the inside, like slits, or windows closed with lattice work.

decisions.choice: palm trees: carved palm-tree decoration
decisions.reason: Palm trees were carved on the walls and doors of Solomon's temple too (1 Kings 6:29-35). With the cherubim of 41:18 they picture a garden, as Eden was guarded by cherubim (Genesis 3:24).

decisions.choice: porches: a rare plural form of the word for porch
decisions.reason: The form is used only in chapter 40 (verses 16, 21-36). It is usually taken as another form of the word for porch, though some read it as the jambs or projecting walls of the porch.

decisions.choice: recessed windows (L, B); windows set deep in their frames (R)
decisions.reason: The same choice as 1 Kings 6:4. Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: carved palm trees (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes it plain that these are decorations (m2).

records.source: וַיְבִיאֵ֗נִי אֶל־הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה לְשָׁכוֹת֙ וְרִֽצְפָ֔ה עָשׂ֥וּי לֶחָצֵ֖ר סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים לְשָׁכ֖וֹת אֶל־הָרִֽצְפָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he brought me into the court, the outer, and look, rooms and a pavement made for the court all around all around; thirty rooms [were] to the pavement.
pieces: Then he brought me into the outer court. There were rooms there, and a pavement laid all around the court; thirty rooms faced the pavement.

L.17: Then he brought me into the outer court, and look, [there were] chambers and a pavement made for the court all around; thirty chambers [faced] onto the pavement.

R.17: Then he took me into the outer courtyard. Around it there were rooms and a stone pavement. Thirty rooms faced the pavement.

decisions.choice: rooms in the outer court: rooms where the people ate their offerings
decisions.reason: The thirty rooms along the outer wall are not explained here. They were probably for the worshipers, to eat the meals of the peace offerings, as the rooms of the temple in Jeremiah 35:2-4 were used. 46:21-24 describes the kitchens in the corners of the same court.

decisions.choice: pavement: a paved stone floor
decisions.reason: The word is used for the paved floor of the court at Solomon's dedication (2 Chronicles 7:3).

decisions.choice: chambers (L); rooms (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is used again and again in chapters 40-46. Literal says "chambers"; Balanced and Readable "rooms".

records.source: וְהָרִֽצְפָה֙ אֶל־כֶּ֣תֶף הַשְּׁעָרִ֔ים לְעֻמַּ֖ת אֹ֣רֶךְ הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים הָרִֽצְפָ֖ה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And the pavement [was] to [the] side of the gates, corresponding to [the] length of the gates, the pavement the lower.
pieces: The pavement ran along the sides of the gates and was as wide as the gates were long. This was the lower pavement.

L.18: And the pavement [ran] beside the gates, matching the length of the gates; [this was] the lower pavement.

R.18: The pavement ran alongside the gates. It was as wide as the gates were long. This was the lower pavement.

decisions.choice: the lower pavement: the pavement of the outer court, lower than the inner court
decisions.reason: The temple stands on a series of terraces. The outer court is reached by seven steps (verse 22) and the inner court by eight more (verse 31), so the pavement of the outer court is the lower one.

records.source: וַיָּ֣מָד רֹ֡חַב מִלִּפְנֵי֩ הַשַּׁ֨עַר הַתַּחְתּ֜וֹנָה לִפְנֵ֨י הֶחָצֵ֧ר הַפְּנִימִ֛י מִח֖וּץ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה הַקָּדִ֖ים וְהַצָּפֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] breadth from before the gate the lower to [the] front of the court the inner from outside, a hundred cubits, the east and the north.
pieces: He measured the distance from the inner front of the lower gate to the outer front of the inner court: it was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}, on the east side and on the north.

L.19: And he measured the width from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court on the outside, a hundred cubits, [on] the east and the north.

R.19: He measured the distance from the lower gate to the outside of the inner courtyard. It was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}, both on the east side and on the north side.

decisions.choice: the east and the north: the measure applies on the east side and is repeated on the north
decisions.reason: The two words end the account of the east gate and lead into the north gate (verse 20). The hundred cubits is the width of the outer court between its gate and the gate of the inner court opposite (verse 23).

decisions.choice: a hundred cubits (L); {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Numbers of a hundred and above are written in figures in the alternative of the units span; Literal says "a hundred cubits".

records.source: וְהַשַּׁ֗עַר אֲשֶׁ֤ר פָּנָיו֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן לֶחָצֵ֖ר הַחִֽיצוֹנָ֑ה מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And the gate whose face [was] [the] way of the north to the court the outer, he measured its length and its breadth.
pieces: Next he measured the length and the width of the gate of the outer court that faces north.

L.20: And the gate of the outer court that faces toward the north: he measured its length and its width.

R.20: Next he measured the length and the width of the north gate of the outer courtyard.

records.source: וְתָאָ֗יו שְׁלוֹשָׁ֤ה מִפּוֹ֙ וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה מִפּ֔וֹ וְאֵילָ֤יו וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙ הָיָ֔ה כְּמִדַּ֖ת הַשַּׁ֣עַר הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אָרְכּ֔וֹ וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים בָּאַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And its alcoves, three from here and three from here, and its jambs and its porches were like [the] measurement of the first gate; fifty cubits [was] its length, and [the] breadth five and twenty by the cubit.
pieces: Its alcoves, three on each side, its jambs and its porch had the same measurements as the first gate. It was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}} wide.

L.21: And its alcoves, three on one side and three on the other, and its jambs and its porches were according to the measurement of the first gate; fifty cubits [was] its length, and twenty-five by the cubit [its] breadth.

R.21: It had three alcoves on each side. Its alcoves, its side posts and its porch were the same size as those of the first gate. It was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: the measurement of the first gate: the north gate is the same as the east gate
decisions.reason: Each gate of the outer court is built to one plan. The repetition stresses the symmetry of the whole temple, which is laid out on a square (42:15-20).

decisions.choice: its porch (B, R)
decisions.reason: The plural form "its porches" (see verse 16) refers to the porch at the end of the gate; Balanced and Readable use the singular, as there is one porch in each gate (verse 8).

records.source: וְחַלּוֹנָ֤יו וְאֵֽלַמָּיו֙ וְתִ֣מֹרָ֔יו כְּמִדַּ֣ת הַשַּׁ֔עַר אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּנָ֖יו דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַקָּדִ֑ים וּבְמַעֲל֥וֹת שֶׁ֨בַע֙ יַֽעֲלוּ־ב֔וֹ וְאֵֽילַמָּ֖יו לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And its windows and its porches and its palm trees [were] like [the] measurement of the gate whose face [was] [the] way of the east; and by seven steps they went up into it, and its porches [were] before them.
pieces: Its windows, its porch and its palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate that faces east. Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end.

L.22: And its windows and its porches and its palm trees [were] according to the measurement of the gate that faces toward the east; and by seven steps people went up into it, and its porches [were] in front of them.

R.22: Its windows, its porch and its palm-tree carvings were like those of the east gate. Seven steps led up to it. Its porch was at the far end, facing the courtyard.

decisions.choice: its porches before them: the porch is at the opposite end from the steps
alternatives: the porch at the top of the steps
decisions.reason: "Before them" may mean "in front of the steps" or "facing them", that is, at the inner end of the gate, where the porch lies (verse 9). In the inner court the order is reversed, and the porch faces outward (verse 31).

decisions.choice: seven steps: the outer court is raised above the ground outside
decisions.reason: The gates of the outer court are reached by seven steps, and those of the inner court by eight (verse 31). The numbers show the temple rising toward its center.

records.source: וְשַׁ֨עַר֙ לֶחָצֵ֣ר הַפְּנִימִ֔י נֶ֣גֶד הַשַּׁ֔עַר לַצָּפ֖וֹן וְלַקָּדִ֑ים וַיָּ֧מָד מִשַּׁ֛עַר אֶל־שַׁ֖עַר מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And a gate to the court the inner [was] opposite the gate to the north and to the east; and he measured from gate to gate a hundred cubits.
pieces: The inner court had a gate opposite the north gate, as it had on the east. He measured from gate to gate: {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}.

L.23: And a gate of the inner court [was] opposite the gate on the north, as on the east; and he measured a hundred cubits from gate to gate.

R.23: The inner courtyard had a gate across from the north gate, just as it did on the east side. He measured from one gate to the other. It was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}.

records.source: וַיּוֹלִכֵ֨נִי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה־שַׁ֖עַר דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֑וֹם וּמָדַ֤ד אֵילָיו֙ וְאֵ֣ילַמָּ֔יו כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And he led me [the] way of the south, and look, a gate [the] way of the south; and he measured its jambs and its porches according to these measurements.
pieces: Then he led me to the south side, and there was a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and its porch, and they had the same measurements as the others.

L.24: Then he led me toward the south, and look, [there was] a gate toward the south; and he measured its jambs and its porches; [they were] according to these measurements.

R.24: Then he led me to the south side. There I saw a gate that faced south. He measured its side posts and its porch. They were the same size as the others.

records.source: וְחַלּוֹנִ֨ים ל֤וֹ וּלְאֵֽילַמָּיו֙ סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֔יב כְּהַחֲלֹּנ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים אַמָּה֙ אֹ֔רֶךְ וְרֹ֕חַב חָמֵ֥שׁ וְעֶשְׂרִ֖ים אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And windows [were] to it and to its porches all around all around like these windows; fifty cubits length, and breadth five and twenty cubits.
pieces: The gate and its porch had windows all around like the other windows. It was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}} wide.

L.25: And [there were] windows in it and in its porches all around, like those windows; fifty cubits [was its] length and the width twenty-five cubits.

R.25: The gate and its porch had windows all around, like the others. It was {{units:about 87 1/2 feet|fifty cubits}} long and {{units:about 43 3/4 feet|twenty-five cubits}} wide.

records.source: וּמַעֲל֤וֹת שִׁבְעָה֙ עֹֽלוֹתָ֔יו וְאֵֽלַמָּ֖יו לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְתִמֹרִ֣ים ל֗וֹ אֶחָ֥ד מִפּ֛וֹ וְאֶחָ֥ד מִפּ֖וֹ אֶל־אֵילָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And steps seven [were] its ascents, and its porches [were] before them; and palm trees [were] to it, one from here and one from here, on its jambs.
pieces: Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the inner end. It had palm trees on its jambs, one on each side.

L.26: And seven steps [were] its ascent, and its porches [were] in front of them; and it [had] palm trees, one on one side and one on the other, on its jambs.

R.26: Seven steps led up to it, and its porch was at the far end. There were carved palm trees on its side posts, one on each side.

records.source: וְשַׁ֛עַר לֶחָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖י דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַדָּר֑וֹם וַיָּ֨מָד מִשַּׁ֧עַר אֶל־הַשַּׁ֛עַר דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַדָּר֖וֹם מֵאָ֥ה אַמּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And a gate [was] to the court the inner [the] way of the south; and he measured from gate to the gate [the] way of the south a hundred cubits.
pieces: The inner court also had a gate facing south. He measured from this gate to the outer gate on the south: {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}.

L.27: And [there was] a gate of the inner court toward the south; and he measured a hundred cubits from gate to gate toward the south.

R.27: The inner courtyard also had a gate on the south side. He measured from that gate to the outer south gate. It was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}.

records.source: וַיְבִיאֵ֛נִי אֶל־חָצֵ֥ר הַפְּנִימִ֖י בְּשַׁ֣עַר הַדָּר֑וֹם וַיָּ֨מָד֙ אֶת־הַשַּׁ֣עַר הַדָּר֔וֹם כַּמִּדּ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And he brought me into [the] court the inner by [the] gate of the south, and he measured the gate the south according to these measurements.
pieces: Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate. He measured the south gate, and it had the same measurements as the others.

L.28: Then he brought me to the inner court through the south gate, and measured the south gate; [it was] according to these measurements.

R.28: Then he took me into the inner courtyard through the south gate. He measured it. It was the same size as the others.

decisions.choice: into the inner court: the tour moves up to the inner court
decisions.reason: The guide now leads Ezekiel up the steps into the inner court. Its three gates mirror the three outer gates (verses 28-37).

decisions.choice: there they rinse the burnt offering: the parts of the animal were washed before they were burned
decisions.reason: The law required the inner parts and legs of a burnt offering to be washed with water before they were burned on the altar (Leviticus 1:9, 13). 2 Chronicles 4:6 speaks of basins for this work in Solomon's temple.

decisions.reason: The plural "gates" is unexpected. The following verses (39-43) describe tables in the porch of a gate and outside "the north gate" (verse 40), so the room is probably beside the inner north gate, though some place it at each inner gate.

decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what was washed.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering: the main animal offerings of the law
decisions.reason: The burnt offering was burned whole on the altar (Leviticus 1). The sin offering (or purification offering) and the guilt offering dealt with sin and its wrongs (Leviticus 4-7). Ezekiel names them without explaining them; the law already did so.

decisions.choice: burnt offering, sin offering, guilt offering (all levels)
decisions.reason: The names used for these offerings in Leviticus 7:37.

On them were placed the tools used for slaughtering the burnt offerings and the other sacrifices.

L.42: And four tables of hewn stone [were] for the burnt offering, [in] length a cubit and a half, [in] breadth a cubit and a half, and [in] height one cubit; on them they laid the implements with which they slaughtered the burnt offering and the sacrifice.

decisions.choice: the sacrifice: the other animal sacrifices, especially the peace offerings
decisions.reason: The word is the general one for an animal sacrifice, often used for the peace offerings that the worshipers ate. Set beside "the burnt offering", it means the other sacrifices.

decisions.choice: a cubit and a half: {{units:about 31 1/2 inches|a cubit and a half}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Worked on the long cubit of verse 5.

decisions.choice: hooks: perhaps double hooks for hanging carcasses, or ledges
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its form looks like a dual ("a pair"). It is usually taken as pegs or double hooks on which the slaughtered animals were hung. Some read it as rims or ledges on the tables. The Septuagint has a different reading here.

decisions.choice: a handbreadth: the width of a hand, about 3 inches
decisions.reason: A handbreadth is a sixth or a seventh of a cubit. On the long cubit of verse 5 it is about 3 inches.

decisions.choice: a handbreadth: about 3 inches (B, R)
decisions.reason: As 1 Kings 7:26.

L.44: And outside the inner gate, in the inner court, [were] the singers' chambers, one [of] which [was] at the side of the north gate, facing toward the south, [and] one at the side of the east gate, facing toward the north.

R.44: Just outside the inner gates, in the inner courtyard, were rooms for the singers. One was beside the north gate and faced south. The other was beside the east gate and faced north.

decisions.choice: rooms of singers: or, following the Septuagint, two rooms
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "rooms of singers". The Septuagint reads "two rooms", which fits what follows ("one ... one") and verses 45-46, where the two rooms are for priests; the Hebrew words for "singers" and "two" look alike. Many think "two rooms" is the original reading, and that the east gate (verse 44) should be "the south gate". The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: keepers of the charge of the house: those who carry out the duties of the temple
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of the Levites' service in Numbers 3:28, 32 and 18:3-5. Here it is the priests who look after the temple buildings, as distinct from those who serve at the altar (verse 46). 44:14-16 makes the same distinction.

decisions.choice: who take care of the temple (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the phrase means (m1).

records.gloss: And the room whose face [is] [the] way of the north [is] for [the] priests, keepers of [the] charge of the altar; they [are] [the] sons of Zadok, the ones approaching from [the] sons of Levi to Yahweh to serve him.
pieces: and the room facing north is for the priests who are in charge of the altar. These are the descendants of Zadok, the only ones among the descendants of Levi who may come near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.46: and the chamber that faces toward the north [is] for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. They [are] the sons of Zadok, who alone from the sons of Levi come near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.46: The room that faces north is for the priests who take care of the altar. They are the descendants of Zadok. Of all the members of the tribe of Levi, only they may come near to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: the sons of Zadok: the priestly family of Zadok
decisions.reason: Zadok was the priest who served David and anointed Solomon (1 Kings 1:32-39; 2:35). His family led the priesthood in the Jerusalem temple. In 44:15-16 the LORD gives them alone the right to serve at the altar, because they stayed faithful when Israel went astray.

decisions.choice: the ones who come near from the sons of Levi: alone of all the Levites
decisions.reason: All the priests were Levites, but not all Levites were priests. The sons of Zadok are the Levites who may come near the LORD at the altar (44:15).

decisions.choice: sons of Zadok (L); descendants of Zadok (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same choice is used for this family through chapters 40-48.

records.source: וַיָּ֨מָד אֶת־הֶחָצֵ֜ר אֹ֣רֶךְ׀מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֛חַב מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּ֖ה מְרֻבָּ֑עַת וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And he measured the court, length a hundred cubits and breadth a hundred cubits, square; and the altar [was] before the house.
pieces: Then he measured the court. It was square, {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long and {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} wide. The altar stood in front of the temple.

L.47: And he measured the court: length a hundred cubits, and breadth a hundred cubits, square; and the altar [was] in front of the house.

R.47: Then he measured the courtyard. It was a square, {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long and {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} wide. The altar stood in front of the temple.

decisions.choice: square: the inner court is a perfect square
decisions.reason: The square is a sign of completeness and order. The whole temple area is a square (42:20), as is the holy portion of the land (48:20). In Revelation 21:16 the holy city is laid out as a square.

decisions.choice: the altar in front of the house: the altar of burnt offering, described in 43:13-17
decisions.reason: The altar stands at the center of the inner court, before the temple building.

records.source: וַיְבִאֵנִי֮ אֶל־אֻלָ֣ם הַבַּיִת֒ וַיָּ֨מָד֙ אֵ֣ל אֻלָ֔ם חָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפֹּ֔ה וְחָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפֹּ֑ה וְרֹ֣חַב הַשַּׁ֔עַר שָׁלֹ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וְשָׁלֹ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he brought me to [the] porch of the house, and he measured [the] jamb of [the] porch, five cubits from here and five cubits from here; and [the] breadth of the gate three cubits from here and three cubits from here.
pieces: Then he brought me to the porch of the temple and measured its jambs: they were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} on each side. The sides of the entrance were {{units:about 5 1/4 feet|three cubits}} wide on each side.

L.48: Then he brought me to the porch of the house, and he measured the jamb of the porch, five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other; and the width of the gate [was] three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.

R.48: Then he took me to the porch of the temple. He measured its side posts. They were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick on each side. The walls beside the doorway were {{units:about 5 1/4 feet|three cubits}} wide on each side.

decisions.choice: the breadth of the gate, three cubits on each side: the Septuagint has a fuller text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads "and the width of the gate was fourteen cubits, and the side walls of the gate were three cubits on each side". The Hebrew may have lost the words for the gate's width. The translation follows the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the porch of the house: the porch of the temple itself
decisions.reason: The tour now reaches the temple building, which is described in 40:48-41:26. Its plan, porch, main hall and inner room follows Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:2-3).

records.source: אֹ֣רֶךְ הָאֻלָ֞ם עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֨חַב֙ עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה אַמָּ֔ה וּבַֽמַּעֲל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲל֖וּ אֵלָ֑יו וְעַמֻּדִים֙ אֶל־הָ֣אֵילִ֔ים אֶחָ֥ד מִפֹּ֖ה וְאֶחָ֥ד מִפֹּֽה׃
records.gloss: [The] length of the porch twenty cubits, and [the] breadth eleven cubits, and by the steps by which they go up to it; and pillars [were] to the jambs, one from here and one from here.
pieces: The porch was {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 19 1/4 feet|eleven cubits}} deep, and steps led up to it. There were pillars beside the jambs, one on each side.

L.49: The length of the porch, twenty cubits, and the breadth, eleven cubits; and by steps [people] went up to it; and [there were] pillars beside the jambs, one on one side and one on the other.

R.49: The porch was {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide and {{units:about 19 1/4 feet|eleven cubits}} deep. Steps led up to it. Beside the side posts there were two pillars, one on each side.

decisions.choice: eleven cubits ... by the steps: the Septuagint reads "twelve cubits" and "ten steps"
decisions.reason: The Septuagint has "twelve" for "eleven" and "by ten steps" for "by the steps". The temple building is reached by a further flight above the inner court (eight steps), as the outer court is by seven and the inner court by eight; ten would complete the rise. The translation keeps the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: pillars, one on each side: like Jachin and Boaz
decisions.reason: Two pillars stood at the porch of Solomon's temple, named Jachin and Boaz (1 Kings 7:15-22). These are not named.

decisions.choice: length twenty, breadth eleven: the porch is twenty cubits across the front and eleven deep
decisions.reason: "Length" here runs across the front of the temple, as in 1 Kings 6:3, where the porch is also twenty cubits across.

decisions.choice: twenty cubits wide and eleven cubits deep (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say which way each measure runs (m3).
